text:
mika: I opened a tiny PR that consolidates rate-limit troubleshooting into a single "mini-handbook" page. Intention: quick checks (429 vs 504), header variants, and 3 short snippets (curl, ruby, js) for inspecting Retry-After and doing a polite fallback. Need a fast review.

rachel: Love the handbook idea. Quick asks: call out header name variations (Retry-After, X-Retry-After, X-Rate-Limit-Reset, X-Retry-After-MS) and show both header parsing and SDK error-code handling (eg code: "rate_limit").

osman: Agree. Also recommend a one-line note about proxies rewriting headers. Add a tiny ruby snippet for variety; ops folks sometimes use ruby.

mika: Draft curl example in the PR:```bash
# show headers to debug rate-limits
curl -i -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{}' | sed -n '1,40p'
```

mika: Ruby example I added:```ruby
# parse Retry-After (seconds) or X-Retry-After-MS (milliseconds)
resp = http.post('/generate', json: body, headers: { 'Authorization' => "Bearer #{ENV['KEY']}" })
ra = resp['Retry-After'] || (resp['X-Retry-After-MS'] && (resp['X-Retry-After-MS'].to_i / 1000))
if ra && ra.to_i > 0
  sleep ra.to_i
  # fallback to cheaper model
  resp = client.generate(model: 'redwood-small', messages: ctx)
end
```

rachel: Nice. For JS streaming, add a note: if you see partial frames followed by a rate-limit marker, check headers for retry window before re-requesting. 504 usually means connection was cut.

osman: Add a short migration note: old key `retry_policy` -> new `backoff_strategy` shape. Show JSON example and call out forgetting jitter as a common pitfall.

mika: Added migration snippet: "\"backoff_strategy\": {\"type\":\"exponential\",\"base_ms\":250,\"max_ms\":8000,\"jitter\":true}" and a small checklist at the top: 1) confirm 429 vs client timeout 2) inspect headers 3) prefer trimming prefix tokens 4) consider model fallback 5) check load-test clients.

mika: Fixed fences and wording, pushed. Re-requesting review.

mika: Thanks all! Will also add a short note in the SDK guide linking the handbook page.
